title: What the Channel Feeds
logline: In a dry-zone village, farmers wait for the tank gate to open, and a single release of water starts a chain that ends, months later, at a bowl of rice on a table none of them will ever see.
human_question: How many hands and how much water does it take before a single meal can exist?

premise.story: One paddy season on a small family plot fed by a shared irrigation tank, from the meeting that decides when the sluice opens to the harvest and the first cooked rice.
premise.place: A tank-fed paddy village in the dry zone, where water is shared by turns and argument.
premise.experience: The long, patient unfolding of a single grain: soil, water, labour, weather and neighbours, each one holding up the next, until a family eats what none of them made alone.

concept_links.why: The Margaya's own image for nutriment: a seed starts the plant, but water and fertiliser keep it growing; a crop visibly depends on many supports at once, none of which it controls.
Water released on a fixed rotation, borrowed labour, seed and weather are each a specific, nameable support for the harvest, not a vague sense that everything is connected.
A farmer's short answer for a good or bad season ('the rain came' or 'it failed') and the long answer, the whole chain of specific supports, are both true at once.

what_camera_could_observe: Seed soaking and the nursery bed
The farmers' meeting deciding the water order, and the channel gate opening
Water reaching the last field in the rotation
Transplanting by hand; fertiliser carried in
The crop's colour changing with water and weather over months
Harvest, milling, and a first cooked meal of the new rice
what_must_be_real: The family's real water-sharing arrangement, their debts and expectations, and the season's real outcome, good or bad.

possible_arc.opening: A dry canal bed and a meeting to decide whose turn the water is.
possible_arc.turn: Water reaches the field, and the crop is now visibly bound to a rotation it does not control.
possible_arc.ending_open: A harvest and a meal, or a season that disappoints; reality decides.

position_hint: opening candidate: matches the group's own opening image of rain to tank to paddy to rice; an Object 9 acquisition (something that exists only because of this whole chain, such as a hand-milled bag of rice or a winnowing basket) would be possible only if it really happens

requirements: A working tank-fed irrigation system with a visible water-sharing arrangement
A family plot that can be followed through most of one season
Willingness to show disputes or hardship honestly, not only a good outcome

suggestions.name: A minor-tank paddy village in the Rajarata dry zone
suggestions.why: Small, tank-fed paddy systems with rotational water sharing are widespread and long-established across this region.
suggestions.season_notes: Yala or Maha cultivation season, depending on the tank
suggestions.verify: A specific tank, family and water-sharing arrangement must be identified and confirmed.

risks: Pastoral cliché; postcard imagery of rural hardship
Treating the farmers as illustrations of doctrine rather than people with real debts, rain and prices
Filming a water dispute as manufactured drama
drop_if: No family willing to show the whole season, including disappointment
No real water-sharing meeting or decision happens within the filming window

connections.note: Both are candidate openings built around acquiring something that exists only because many hands and processes made it.
The rice grown here could plausibly be part of the shared meal followed in 'What the Meal Leaves Behind'.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
